findings.claim: The manifest selects BLE for iOS for both PLYR720 variants. It selects Bluetooth Classic and LE Audio for Android.
Product 0x29 is S6PCW, uses the SG200 firmware family, and advertises SG200-Slave and Crusher PLYR aliases. Product 0x2A is S6PXW, uses SG200X, and advertises SG200X-Slave.
The manifest lists separate Master and Slave download URLs. The highest listed firmware version is v1.0.0.34 for both products. Version 1.0.0.35 does not occur in these product records.

The entries require minAppVersion 3.7.6, enable updates on iOS and Android, and set androidPollingIntervalSeconds to 5. Some early entries point to an unavailable placeholder. The manifest does not prove that any URL currently serves data.

The strings identify SG200 EQ mapping and stored EQ array-index builders, THX state/read/write builders, FotaPackage, and CRC confirmation builders. The strings do not establish command bytes or firmware encryption.
findings.status: source-confirmed; interpretation limited to string presence

gaps: The selected product records contain no Bluetooth service UUID or explicit RACE transport configuration.
The Master/Slave role names are manifest labels. These records do not establish their internal chip topology.
The aux strings may describe button actions or generic audio state. Their presence does not establish a powered aux routing command.
ENCRYPTED_SIZE and _isBufferEncrypted are generic string leads. Their presence does not prove that the firmware binaries use encryption.
The Dart binary needs method recovery to identify command opcodes, payload formats, and model-selection paths.
No secrets assets were read. No URL was fetched. No hardware traffic was sent.
